title: Rigveda 10.178: To Tarksya
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 (1711 CE (colophon: Saṃvat 1768)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 10.178: To Tarksya: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of a 1711 Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 10.178 is a hymn of 3 verses addressed to Tarksya. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 10, the last and latest book. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 (University of Pennsylvania), a paper manuscript of the eighth aṣṭaka (RV 10.46-10.191) of the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā in Devanāgarī, 158 leaves, 6 lines to the page, with the accents marked in red; the scribe's colophon on fol. 158 gives Saṃvat 1768 (1711 CE); this hymn stands on fol. 150v-151r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Like most Rigveda manuscripts, Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 writes a repeated refrain in short form after its first occurrence (for example kasmai° for kasmai devāya haviṣā vidhema); the Sanskrit shown is the full text of Aufrecht's edition.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).

translation.original_ref: RV 10.178.1-3 (aṣṭaka 8, adhyāya 8, varga 36); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 fol. 151r
translation.original_text:
1tyam ū̱ ṣu vā̱jina̍ṁ de̱vajū̍taṁ sa̱hāvā̍naṁ taru̱tāra̱ṁ rathā̍nām | ari̍ṣṭanemim pṛta̱nāja̍m ā̱śuṁ sva̱staye̱ tārkṣya̍m i̱hā hu̍vema ||
2indra̍syeva rā̱tim ā̱johu̍vānāḥ sva̱staye̱ nāva̍m i̱vā ru̍hema | urvī̱ na pṛthvī̱ bahu̍le̱ gabhī̍re̱ mā vā̱m etau̱ mā pare̍tau riṣāma ||
3sa̱dyaś ci̱d yaḥ śava̍sā̱ pañca̍ kṛ̱ṣṭīḥ sūrya̍ iva̱ jyoti̍ṣā̱pas ta̱tāna̍ | sa̱ha̱sra̱sāḥ śa̍ta̱sā a̍sya̱ raṁhi̱r na smā̍ varante yuva̱tiṁ na śaryā̍m ||
translation.text:
1THIS very mighty one whom Gods commission, the Conqueror of cars, ever triumphant, Swift, fleet to battle, with uninjured fellies, even Târkshya for our weal will we call hither.
2As though we offered up our gifts to Indra, may we ascend. him as a ship. for safety. Like the two wide worlds, broad, deep far-extended, may we be safe both when he comes and leaves you.
3He who with might the Five Lands hath pervaded, like Sûrya with his lustre, and the waters- His strength wins hundreds, thousands none avert it, as- the young maid repelleth not her lover.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48, fol. 151r (OPenn image 150, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 10.178.1 ‹sahāvānaṁ tarutāraṁ rathānām›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 151v, begins in RV 10.179.2 ‹vimadhyam›. Verses 10.178.1-3 end on this page; 10.178.1 begins on fol. 150v.
